homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym, and T composes no other entity under the name. 'EROL' is the census's other name for the entity and the contents page's own ('Contact EROL Administrator'); www.marxists.org/history/erol/ is its path. The distinct entities below are named by the field, the census or #1725 beside the entity and are never senses of its name.
distinct_entities: the Marxists Internet Archive (MIA, marxists.org), its host and parent source (B4 F23; census relations part_of), to whose Wikipedia article the name redirects (B8 F42); a census entity of its own with its own /non row, datasets/negative-of-the-negative/v2/rows/marxists-internet-archive.json, composed in parallel on 2026-10-31 (neither read nor edited)
the 'Encyclopedia of Marxism', another reference section of the MIA (B8 F45), which the census distinguishes ('NOT a general encyclopedia of Marxism', ML-30)
anti-revisionism, the trend it records (B2 F11, F12), a movement distinct from the encyclopedia
the New Communist Movement and the parties and periodicals it documents (B1 F4, F5; B5 F31), among them the Progressive Labor Party and its Challenge/Desafio
the Digital Handbook for Research on Soviet History, Davis Center for Russian and Eurasian Studies, Harvard University, the catalogue of card 4 (B4 F29)
Paul C., who signs the definition page (B2 F20), a person; the EROL Administrator, its contact (B1 F10), unnamed
the REP collective, SDS, Progressive Labor, RYM II and Weatherman, the parties of #1725's SDS case (D1725-01, D1725-02)
BannedThought.net, a neighbour in the census (its own row, bannedthought, composed in parallel; neither read nor edited)

captures.description: THE ENCYCLOPEDIA, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'The Encyclopedia of Anti-Revisionism On-Line (EROL) is a digital archive developed by the Marxists Internet Archive containing primary source documents, translations, and organizational records from the international anti-revisionist and Marxist-Leninist/Maoist movements.' Core definition; timeframe 1946 to 1983; geographic coverage; periodicals. Five cards: three Marxists Internet Archive pages, Harvard University, one more MIA page.
